turns.t: Hello! This is Bella, she's six, and she gets tummy aches before school, every morning, and I'm at my wits' end.
Hello Bella. Can you tell me about your tummy? ~
It hurts. Here.
When does it hurt?
Not at school. ~
She means weekdays, doctor. Monday to Friday, before school, then it goes by the time we get there, and she's running about by break.
And on Saturdays and Sundays? ~
Fine. Never a problem. ~
Bella, do you like school? ~
Yes. I love it. ~
She says that, but she cries when I leave her at the gate, doctor.
I don't cry.
You do, sweetheart, you cry every morning.
I'll write down that Bella says she doesn't cry and Mum says she does. Bella, is there anything about school that's difficult, or any person who's unkind?
No. ~
Does your tummy ever hurt when you do a poo, or when you eat? ~
No. ~
Her bowels are regular, and she eats breakfast, if she can. ~
Let me feel your tummy, Bella. Lie back, it'll tickle. ~
Hee hee.
Her tummy is soft, and there's no tenderness anywhere, even when I press deep.
Is it something physical? ~
Nothing here worries me. Children often get a real tummy ache in the morning when they're a bit anxious about separating from you, and it goes once they're distracted. ~
I feel terrible. ~
Please don't. It's very common at this age, and it's not your fault. ~
What can I do? ~
A calm, consistent goodbye routine, and a firm, kind drop-off. Don't linger. And talk to her teacher so they can greet her at the gate.
I do linger. I give her a hundred cuddles. ~
One big cuddle, a quick wave, and off you go. ~
Mummy, I'll be good. ~
You are good, Bella. And I'd like to arrange a urine test, just to rule out a simple infection that could be causing tummy aches.
Okay. Can she do it here? ~
Yes, the nurse will give you a little pot. ~
Thank you. ~
I'd like to see you again in three weeks, to see how the mornings are going.
Three weeks. Thanks, doctor. ~

chief_complaint.value: she gets tummy aches before school

clinical_uncertainties.description: Child says she does not cry at school drop-off; her mother says she cries every morning (unresolved).

clinical_actions.description: Calm consistent goodbye routine and speak to the teacher about a gate greeting
